Class MCS

java.lang.Object
org.openscience.cdk.isomorphism.MCS
public final class MCS extends Object
Finds the maximum common substructure (MCS) of a query and a target molecule: the connected common substructure with the most atoms and, of those, the most common bonds. The common substructure need not be induced: a bond present on only one side, or whose matching fails, is left out. Every compatible bond between mapped atom pairs is common, and these common bonds keep the mapped atoms connected. A result is a mapping with one entry per query atom, the index of the target atom it maps to or -1. For example, N-methylacetamide CC(=O)NC and propanamide CCC(=O)N, neither a substructure of the other, share an acetamide CC(=O)N. With the first as the query, the only maximum mapping is [1, 2, 3, 4, -1], which leaves out the methyl on the nitrogen.

Usage: 
MCS mcs = MCS.find(query).withTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
int[] mapping = mcs.match(target);     // Intractable after 10 seconds
for (int i = 0; i < mapping.length; i++) {
    if (mapping[i] >= 0) {
        // query.getAtom(i) is mapped to target.getAtom(mapping[i])
    }
}

// the maximum mappings, e.g. both ways round a ring
for (int[] p : mcs.matchAll(target)) {
    // p is a mapping as above
}

// the best mapping found within the 10 seconds, and whether the search finished
MCS.Result result = mcs.search(target);
if (!result.complete()) {
    // result.mapping() may be smaller than the MCS
}
Each with... method returns a new instance and leaves the old one as it is. An instance keeps no other state, so one instance can be used for many targets and shared between threads, except for queries with recursive SMARTS in two threads at once.
  • withCompleteRings() maps rings only whole.
  • withStereochemistry() checks stereochemistry.
  • withDisconnected(int) finds a maximum common edge subgraph, whose common bonds may form several fragments.
Matching

By default atoms match by symbol, so pseudo atoms (R groups, *) match each other and no other atom, and bonds match if both are aromatic, or both are not aromatic and have the same order. With withMatching(Expr.Type...) atoms and bonds match by the expressions QueryAtomContainer.create(IAtomContainer, Expr.Type...) builds from the query instead, for example:
  • ELEMENT: atoms by element, bond orders ignored; a pseudo atom of the query matches any atom, and an element does not match a pseudo atom of the target;
  • ELEMENT, SINGLE_OR_AROMATIC: like the default, except for pseudo atoms;
  • ELEMENT, SINGLE_OR_AROMATIC, IS_IN_RING, IS_IN_CHAIN: like the default, and ring atoms and bonds map only to ring atoms and bonds, chain atoms and bonds only to chain ones (set the ring flags of both molecules first);
  • ELEMENT, SINGLE_OR_AROMATIC, FORMAL_CHARGE (or ISOTOPE): like the default, and the charge (mass number) of a query atom, where it is set, must agree.
A query molecule, for example one parsed from SMARTS, is matched by its own atom and bond predicates (IQueryAtom, IQueryBond). These are evaluated without the configuration of the overall mapping, so top-level SMARTS stereochemistry is not checked, and withStereochemistry() applies only to molecule queries. A recursive SMARTS predicate is evaluated as a substructure search of its own, including its stereochemistry. The result is the largest connected part satisfying these predicates. The target must be a molecule, not a query, prepared as for a SMARTS search. 
IAtomContainer query = builder.newAtomContainer();
Smarts.parse(query, "c1ccccc1C(=O)[N,O]");
SmartsPattern.prepare(target);
int[] mapping = MCS.find(query).match(target);
Preparing the molecules
  • Aromaticity and ring flags are used as they are set. Perceive aromaticity with the same model on both molecules.
  • Explicit hydrogens are atoms like any other: they count in the score, so the heavy atoms of such an MCS can differ from the heavy-atom MCS, and they multiply the number of equally good mappings. Suppress them for a heavy-atom MCS.
  • For molecule queries, stereochemistry is checked only with withStereochemistry(), from the stereo elements as set.
Limits

The search is exact. Large or highly symmetric molecules can take a long time, so a time limit is recommended; there is none by default. When the time runs out or the thread is interrupted, match(IAtomContainer) and matchAll(IAtomContainer) throw Intractable, while search(IAtomContainer) and searchAll(IAtomContainer) return the best mappings found so far, see MCS.Result. matchAll(IAtomContainer) returns at most 1000 mappings, matchAll(IAtomContainer, int) as many as asked for.

Molecules too large to search are refused: the match and search methods then throw IllegalArgumentException without searching. A search of more than 230 atom pairs, query atoms times target atoms (about 32,000 atoms in each molecule), is refused. Searches requiring more than Integer.MAX_VALUE entries in a bond adjacency or compatibility table are also refused. With withCompleteRings(), so is a ring system with more than 1024 relevant rings, or a very large fused one such as a graphene sheet.

    • withMatching

      public MCS withMatching(Expr.Type... opts)
      Match atoms and bonds with the expressions that QueryAtomContainer.create(IAtomContainer, Expr.Type...) makes from the query and opts, at the start of each search. For example withMatching(ELEMENT) ignores bond orders, and withMatching(ELEMENT, IS_IN_RING) also maps ring atoms and bonds of the query only to ring atoms and bonds. Without any types every atom and bond matches. STEREOCHEMISTRY has no effect, see withStereochemistry().
      Parameters:
      opts - the expression types to match
      Returns:
      a new MCS search with this matching
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - the query has query atoms or bonds, which are matched by their own expressions

    • withTimeout

      public MCS withTimeout(long time, TimeUnit unit)
      Stop each search that runs longer than the given time: match(IAtomContainer) and matchAll(IAtomContainer) then throw Intractable, while search(IAtomContainer) and searchAll(IAtomContainer) return the best mappings found so far, see MCS.Result.complete(). The limit is checked as the search runs, including while it is set up, so a search can take slightly longer. Building the query and target graphs beforehand, and the query expressions of withMatching(Expr.Type...), is not counted.
      Parameters:
      time - the time limit, greater than zero
      unit - the unit of the time limit
      Returns:
      a new MCS search with this time limit
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - the time limit is not greater than zero

    • withCompleteRings

      public MCS withCompleteRings()
      Map rings only whole: a ring atom or ring bond of either molecule is in the common substructure only as part of a ring of that molecule whose bonds are all common. This covers every common ring bond, including additional bonds between mapped atoms. So ring atoms and bonds map only onto ring ones, chain onto chain, and a lone ring atom, such as the ring carbon a substituent is attached to, is left out. Rings are the relevant rings [Vismara, Philippe. Combinatorics. 1997. 4], those of every smallest set of smallest rings: benzene is a whole ring of naphthalene, cyclohexane is not one of norbornane. This option neither reads nor sets ring flags. Perceive aromaticity first: under the default matching, a ring drawn with other alternating single and double bonds is not whole. The rings are found as the graphs are built, which the time limit does not cover, so a very large fused ring system can take seconds before the search starts.
      Returns:
      a new MCS search that maps only complete rings

    • withStereochemistry

      public MCS withStereochemistry()
      Check stereochemistry: a mapping must keep the configuration of each tetrahedral centre and double bond that both molecules specify, as far as the mapped atoms fix it. A centre is fixed once it and three of its neighbours are mapped onto a centre and its neighbours, a double bond once both ends and a neighbour of each end are. The arrangement of the mapped neighbours is compared, not CIP labels. A configuration that only one molecule specifies matches either way, and a racemic or relative group, as read from a molfile without the chiral flag, may be inverted as a whole. Other stereochemistry, such as allenes and atropisomers, is not checked. This is a hard constraint: a mapping that fixes a configuration the other way round is not admissible at all, so the result is the largest stereo-consistent match, which can be smaller than the MCS found without this option.
      Returns:
      a new MCS search that checks stereochemistry
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - the query has query atoms or bonds, as this option applies only to molecule queries

    • withDisconnected

      public MCS withDisconnected(int minBonds)
      Find a maximum common edge subgraph [Raymond02 (not found in db)] instead: the mapping with the most common bonds and, of those, the most atoms. The common bonds may form several fragments, each a connected piece of at least minBonds common bonds, anywhere in either molecule. An atom without a common bond is not mapped. A changed linker or a broken bond then costs only the bonds involved. Under the default matching a bond whose order changes is not common, so for reaction mapping ignore bond orders with withMatching(ELEMENT). This search is slower than the connected one, so set a time limit.
      Parameters:
      minBonds - the fewest common bonds of a fragment, at least 1
      Returns:
      a new MCS search for disconnected fragments
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - minBonds is less than 1

    • match

      public int[] match(IAtomContainer target) throws Intractable
      Find a maximum common substructure of the query and the target. The mapping has one entry per query atom: the index of the target atom it is mapped to, or -1 if the atom is not in the common substructure. If there is no common substructure, for example no atom in common, an empty array is returned, where MCS.Result.mapping() has every entry -1.
      Parameters:
      target - the target molecule
      Returns:
      the mapping from the query to the target atoms
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - the molecules are too large to search
      Intractable - the time limit was reached or the thread was interrupted

      Find every maximum common substructure mapping of the query and the target, up to 1000 of them; symmetric molecules can have far more. All have the same number of atoms and common bonds.
      Parameters:
      target - the target molecule
      Returns:
      the mappings from the query to the target atoms, see match(IAtomContainer); an unmodifiable list, empty if there is no common substructure
      Throws:

      Intractable - the time limit was reached or the thread was interrupted

    • matchAll

      public List<int[]> matchAll(IAtomContainer target, int limit) throws Intractable
      Find maximum common substructure mappings of the query and the target, at most limit of them. Each is a maximum mapping, and if there are no more than limit, all of them are returned; matchAll(IAtomContainer) has a limit of 1000. A smaller limit can end the search sooner.
      Parameters:
      target - the target molecule
      limit - the most mappings to return, greater than zero
      Returns:
      the mappings from the query to the target atoms, see match(IAtomContainer); an unmodifiable list, empty if there is no common substructure
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - the limit is not greater than zero, or the molecules are too large to search
      Intractable - the time limit was reached or the thread was interrupted

    • search

      public MCS.Result search(IAtomContainer target)
      Find a maximum common substructure of the query and the target, and return the best mapping found even when the time limit ends the search first. MCS.Result.mapping() has one entry per query atom, the target atom it is mapped to or -1, and MCS.Result.complete() tells whether the search finished, which proves the mapping maximum. For example: 
      MCS.Result result = MCS.find(query).withTimeout(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS).search(target);
int[] mapping = result.mapping();   // the best mapping found within a second
if (!result.complete()) {
    // the time ran out: a larger common substructure may exist
}
      Parameters:
      target - the target molecule
      Returns:
      the best mapping found and whether the search finished
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - the molecules are too large to search
